output.answer: Yes. As of November 11, 2026, Ford has disclosed ongoing employee-separation and restructuring actions: its latest quarterly filing says 2026 charges are expected to be $500 million–$1 billion, primarily attributable to employee separations, with many programs in Europe. Separately, WDR reported on September 22 that 500 employees still had to leave Ford’s Cologne operation under an existing cost-cutting program, while a union update dated October 31 said Ford would recall 18 workers from indefinite layoff on November 2—so layoffs and recalls are both occurring, but Ford has not disclosed one global layoff headcount.
caveats: Ford's latest filing gives a projected cost range, not a single global number of employees to be laid off.

The 500-person Cologne figure is reported as the remaining portion of an earlier program and should not be added to the 750 production-job reduction as a separate total without further reconciliation.
The union update concerns one Canadian facility and reports recalls from indefinite layoff; it does not establish Ford's companywide layoff count.

output.question: Has Ford announced layoffs?

key_facts.fact: Ford's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 says it estimates total 2026 charges of $500 million to $1 billion related to initiated actions, primarily attributable to employee separations; it says some plans remain subject to negotiations.
Ford's latest filing says the separation programs are primarily hourly and salaried worker programs in Europe and are expected to be substantially complete by the end of 2027.

WDR reported that 500 employees at Ford's Cologne operation still had to leave with severance; the report said these positions were part of a previously announced cost-cutting program, not additional cuts, and also mentioned 750 production jobs removed after a shift reduction.
Unifor Local 707 reported that Ford would recall 18 members from indefinite layoff on November 2, 2026, to support Final Assembly manpower needs.
